name: ActualLab.Rpc (part of ActualLab.Fusion)
workload: RPC call throughput (calls/second) and streaming item throughput (items/second) between client and server, measured in-process/local benchmark harness
claimed_speedup: ActualLab.Rpc: 9.91M calls/s vs gRPC 1.28M calls/s (~7.7x) and SignalR 4.85M calls/s (~2x); streaming: 99.96M items/s vs gRPC 43.78M items/s (~2.3x) and SignalR 17.97M items/s (~5.6x). README states "2-7x faster than gRPC and SignalR even in its 'raw' mode"
tradeoffs: .NET/C# only; part of a larger real-time framework (Fusion) with its own caching/pub-sub model, so adopting ActualLab.Rpc in isolation is less common; API differs substantially from gRPC's contract-first model
caveats: First-party benchmark: no CPU/hardware spec, no methodology (payload sizes, client/server topology) given on the README beyond the summary table; no link to a separate reproducible benchmark harness or independent verification found via HN. Could not find a related Hacker News story specifically about this project via HN Algolia search.
found_via: Hacker News: query "gRPC alternative" surfaced no direct hit, but repo was found by following up on "fastest RPC" style searches and directly checking github.com/ActualLab/Fusion (formerly Stl.Fusion), whose HN-linked Notion post "Stl.Rpc: the fastest RPC protocol for .NET (+ benchmarks)" (https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search?query=Stl.Rpc, HN objectID 38568563) pointed to the successor project

name: Exposed (reflectionless RPC for Go)
workload: RPC round-trip calls at payload sizes 8/128/1024/32768/65536 bytes, concurrency levels 1/5/10 clients, load 1-50000 ops, server and client on same machine
claimed_speedup: At 8-byte payload / 50 concurrent ops: Exposed 527,199.3 op/s vs gRPC 394,620.7 op/s (~1.34x); memory 472MB vs 1.4GB; GC cycles 111 vs 538. README states Exposed outperforms gRPC across nearly all tested scenarios.
tradeoffs: Go only; reflectionless codec requires code generation via the 'expose' tool; niche adoption, very small community (3 forks, 27 stars)
caveats: Abandoned since 2018 (7+ years, no activity). Hardware/CPU is stated but exact Go version and compiler flags are not; benchmark source code itself does not appear to be published in the repo (only the results table), so this is a first-party partial-methodology benchmark -> capped at Tier C per rules even though CPU is disclosed. Speedup magnitude (~1.3x) is modest/plausible, not inflated.
found_via: Hacker News: query "high performance RPC framework" -> "Exposed – minimal high performance RPC framework" (https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search?query=high%20performance%20RPC%20framework)

name: AtomicLinkRPC (ALR)
workload: RPC calls with small/medium/large messages (2/9/14 fields) and 100-item collections; RoundTrip and server-streaming patterns; 1-thread and 100-thread client concurrency; localhost and remote (2.5Gbps LAN) topologies
claimed_speedup: Localhost, 1 thread: RoundTripStringAsyncCB 3,761,550 RPC/s (ALR) vs 34,386 RPC/s (gRPC) (~109x); RoundTripSmallMsgAsyncCB ~97x; StreamSmallMsgFromServer ~335x. At 100 threads: ALR 16.0M-65.5M RPC/s vs gRPC 245K-393K RPC/s. HN Show/Ask post states "Benchmark results show that ALR can significantly outperform gRPC".
hardware: Localhost: Dell Alienware Aurora R16, Intel Core i9-14900KF (24C/32T), 64GB RAM, Windows 11. Remote client: Microsoft Surface Laptop Studio, Intel Core i7-11370H @3.30GHz, 32GB RAM, Windows 11; 2.5Gbps Ethernet link.
tradeoffs: Closed/pre-release: the GitHub repo (AtomicLinkRPC/alr-preview) contains only documentation (mkdocs site, README, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, LICENSE-DOCS.md) and no source code for the ALR library itself or its gRPC comparison harness; only docs are covered by LICENSE-DOCS.md, the software has no stated license and is not downloadable/buildable
caveats: Numbers are extremely implausible (up to ~335x for a like-for-like RPC comparison) with no compiler, build flags, or gRPC configuration disclosed, and no independently runnable benchmark code -- per the task's hard rule this caps evidence at Tier C and the magnitude should be treated with strong skepticism (likely misconfigured gRPC baseline, e.g. debug build, no connection reuse, or apples-to-oranges async semantics). Project is a pre-release/preview product (contact email alr-project@alienworks.com) with no public library source, 0 GitHub stars, so notability for a Tier D fallback would not apply either; included here only because it directly names gRPC with numeric claims. Treat as a lead to investigate further, not a verified result.
found_via: Hacker News: query "RPC framework benchmark" -> "Ask HN: Feedback on a new framework aiming at the classic RPC headaches" by thefastpath, 2025-09-08, linking to https://atomiclinkrpc.github.io/alr-preview/
